text.p: Conceptus Inc said Monday it received a letter from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration about the regulatory classification of falloposcopes used to evaluate proximal tubal occlusion in the fallopian tube.
The letter says that the FDA has decided that the falloposcopy devices will be reviewed for marketing through the 510(k) process instead of the more lengthy PMA process.

"FDA's letter does not necessarily indicate that our pending 510(k) will be cleared, nor does it clarify whether additional clinical data will be required before clearance can be obtained," said Cindy Domescus of Conceptus.

"However, we have strongly held that a 510(k) submission is the correct approach for this falloposcopy indication, and we are very pleased that FDA has confirmed this approach, which represents a fundamental policy change regarding the requirements for marketing falloposcopy devices for this indication," she added.
Conceptus originally proposed to the FDA that it downclassify these devices in October of 1995.
Shares of Conceptus were 1-3/4 higher at 10-1/2 in midday trading on Nasdaq.
